name: Energy performance contract: guaranteed savings
summary: An energy service company implements efficiency measures and guarantees a minimum level of savings. If savings fall short it compensates the customer; the customer usually finances the project.
how_it_makes_money: Fee for project delivery and service, tied to the guaranteed savings level; savings above the guarantee may be split with the customer.

hardware: Efficiency measures installed in the building or plant
software: Monitoring and measurement and verification tooling
sites_assets: Customer buildings or facilities, often public
partners: Banks or financiers lending to the customer
financing: Usually customer-financed, with the ESCO guarantee supporting the loan
channel: Tenders and direct sales to public and commercial owners

stakeholder_value.customer: Guaranteed bill reduction with performance risk moved to the ESCO
stakeholder_value.provider: Project and service revenue, upside above the guarantee

what_must_be_true: Baseline and verification method are agreed up front
Real savings reliably exceed the guarantee with a safety buffer
Customer is creditworthy and can finance the project

risks_failure_causes.text: Disagreement on baseline adjustments or measured savings
ESCO must compensate the customer if savings fall below the guarantee
Public agencies may lack procurement rules or understanding for performance contracting

cases.note: Guaranteed savings is reported as the most common EPC type in Europe and heavily used in North America, Africa, the Middle East and Australia.
